policy_title: Public Health Approach to Youth Violence
stated: Address youth violence and combat knife crime by: Adopting a public health approach to the epidemic of youth violence which identifies and treats risk factors. Investing in youth services that are genuinely engaging and reach more young people. Making youth diversion a statutory duty so that every part of the country has a pre-charge diversion scheme for young people up to the age of 25.

source.quote: Address youth violence and combat knife crime by: Adopting a public health approach to the epidemic of youth violence which identifies and treats risk factors, rather than just focusing on the symptoms. This means police, teachers, health professionals, youth workers and social services all working closely together to prevent young people falling prey to gangs and violence. Investing in youth services that are genuinely engaging and reach more young people. Making youth diversion a statutory duty so that every part of the country has a pre-charge diversion scheme for young people up to the age of 25, ensuring better outcomes for young people and less strain on police resources.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets youth violence and knife crime through prevention, diversion and a public-health risk-factor model — all core crime, policing and justice indicators under O5.

Pre-charge diversion protects young people from criminal records that are a major barrier to education, training and employment; investment in 'genuinely engaging' youth services explicitly aims to re-route at-risk young people toward legitimate opportunity pathways, moving the attainment-gap and opportunity indicators.

Youth knife crime is a demonstrated driver of eroded social trust and community fear in affected neighbourhoods; the community-based public-health framing and youth-services investment are specifically designed to rebuild belonging and inter-group relations, moving social-trust and civic-participation indicators.

membership_note: Three bearings are justified: O5 is the explicit safety target; O7 captures the opportunity-pathway effect of diversion and youth-services investment on at-risk young people's futures; O15 captures the community-trust dimension that is both damaged by youth violence and targeted by the community-engagement strand of the policy.
